title: AI Friction
notes_h2: When is a drill not a drill?
notes_html:
The carpenter. A carpenter helping put in our new kitchen cabinets asked me, "Greg, when is a drill not a drill?" Then he used the drill to lightly tap a cabinet into alignment, grinned, and said, "When it's a hammer." Sometimes it doesn't make sense to walk to the toolbox. Just get the job done.

Ore is not gold. More polished output with no impact is more ore, not more gold. Usage counts measure the ore.

Not the same as. Avoid AI Slop keeps AI output genuine when you do use it; this pattern asks whether to use it. Right Tool, Right Job chooses among tools; this one is about the habit of reaching for AI by default.

Related. A value statement from Begin with the End in Mind exposes zero-impact work. Inflated output also flattens voices (Ten People, One Idea).
strip: Paste this into any AI system's custom instructions or at the start of a conversation to run AI Friction. It tells you when you don't need AI for the job, keeps the person in personal work, and helps fully where AI has real leverage.
